findings.text: When the same field appears 3+ times (e.g., foo=a&foo=b&foo=c), line 43 wraps the existing array with the new value, producing nested arrays [[a,b],c] instead of flat [a,b,c]
No prototype pollution protection: formData entry __proto__[polluted]=value parses to [__proto__,polluted] and sets Object.prototype.polluted, allowing attackers to inject properties into all objects

0.reason: The code wraps an existing value in an array on each duplicate key, so a third occurrence nests the previous array, producing [[a,b],c] instead of a flat array.

1.reason: The code directly assigns parsed path segments as object keys without checking for __proto__, allowing prototype pollution via formData entries.
